newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebel leader returns to Zaire from S.Africa talks.
newsitem.headline: Rebel leader returns to Zaire from S.Africa talks.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila returned to Lubumbashi on Thursday from Cape Town after talks in South Africa about his civil war to unseat Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko.

Kabila, who has suddenly appeared shy of the media, refused to leave the South African Air Force Lear jet that had brought him until his security men and soldiers cleared television crews from the tarmac.
Rebel leader returns to Zaire from S.Africa talks

It was not clear if he would, as expected earlier, address the people of Lubumbashi -- Zaire's second city and his greatest conquest to date -- at a victory rally in the afternoon. The city was taken by rebels more than a week ago.

In Cape Town, South African President Nelson Mandela said after the departure of Kabila that his talks with the Zaire rebel leader and Mobutu left him confident of a peaceful end to Zaire's civil war.

"I have been speaking both to (rebel) president (Laurent) Kabila and to (Zairean) President Mobutu, and as a result of the exchanges I have had with them, and the other leaders in Africa, I am confident that a peaceful solution will be achieved," Mandela told reporters.
African elder statesman Mandela, who held an hour-long session on Wednesday evening with Kabila, said he had also spoken to Mobutu three times since last Saturday.
